docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Last updated: June 30, 2026

CicloBeef Studio respects the privacy of its clients, collaborators and visitors.

This page explains what personal data may be collected through our website, Instagram DM, Facebook Page DM, LinkedIn, email and order channels, how it may be used and which rights you have regarding your information.

docs.title: What Data We Collect
docs.text:
Depending on the request, quote or contact channel, we may collect:

  • Name and surname.
  • Email address and phone number, when provided or required for the order.
  • Country, region, city, postal code and shipping address.
  • Message content, artwork request, studio edition type, size, orientation, quantity and quote details.
  • Order information, payment status, delivery status and tracking information.
  • Communications sent by Instagram DM, Facebook Page DM, LinkedIn, email or other listed contact channels.

We do not intentionally collect sensitive personal data through our public website.

docs.title: How We Use Your Data
docs.text:
We may use the information you provide to:

  • Respond to inquiries, messages and collaboration proposals.
  • Prepare personalized quotes based on studio edition, format, destination, shipping and applicable order conditions.
  • Confirm orders and PayPal payment status.
  • Produce, print, fulfill and dispatch made-to-order studio editions.
  • Provide delivery updates, tracking information and customer support.
  • Investigate order issues, damaged studio editions, missing items or delivery problems.
  • Maintain legitimate commercial, accounting and support records.

CicloBeef Studio uses internal records and operational tools to manage inventory, quotes and sales history. We do not publish internal spreadsheet names, formulas or system architecture in public documentation.

We do not sell your data to third parties.

docs.title: Service Providers and External Channels
docs.text:
Only the data strictly necessary for an order or request may be shared with external providers.

This may include:

  • External print, production and fulfillment providers, when needed to produce and deliver an order.
  • Shipping carriers and logistics providers, when needed for delivery and tracking.
  • Communication, storage, form and email providers, when those services are used for a specific request or order.
  • PayPal, when a customer approves a quote and receives a payment link for the final order total.
  • Instagram DM and Facebook Page DM, operated by Meta, when you contact CicloBeef Studio through those channels.
  • LinkedIn, when you use that channel for contracts, professional coordination or related administrative matters.

These providers may process data in countries other than your own. Because CicloBeef Studio may prepare and deliver orders internationally, personal data may be transferred or processed internationally for quoting, production, fulfillment, shipping, support and recordkeeping.

docs.title: Cookies and Analytics
docs.text:
The current public website repository does not show active CicloBeef Studio cookies or analytics tools. If those tools are added later, this policy should be updated before they are presented as active.

Third-party platforms that you choose to use, such as Instagram DM, Facebook Page DM, LinkedIn or PayPal, may apply their own privacy, cookie or analytics practices under their own policies.

docs.title: Data Storage, Retention and Security
docs.text:
• Data may be stored in email systems, internal records, order documents and operational tools used by CicloBeef Studio.
  • We keep personal data only for as long as necessary to manage the relationship, prepare and complete orders, comply with legal obligations, resolve incidents and maintain legitimate business records.
  • We take reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect personal data; however, no method of transmission or storage is 100% secure.

docs.title: Your Rights
docs.text:
You may request:

  • Access to the personal data we hold about you.
  • Correction of inaccurate or outdated information.
  • Deletion of your data from our records, unless we are legally required or otherwise allowed to keep it for legitimate purposes.

To do so, please email us at:

ciclobeefstudio@gmail.com

docs.title: Mission
docs.text: To connect people worldwide with history and society through premium artistic creations that combine visual excellence, research and critical reflection.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: To build a catalog of artworks and visual narratives that can be exhibited, collected and integrated into projects led by museums, institutions, foundations and private collectors around the world.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Offer high-quality, curated art pieces with strong historical and social content.
  • Provide a professional and reliable experience to international clients.
  • Document our work transparently and with academic rigor.
  • Prepare the technical foundation to integrate automation tools (e.g. Meta Graph API) into our communication and services.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Ciclobeef Studio operates with an international focus:

  • Geographical scope: North America, Europe, Latin America and other regions open to premium framed art and curated visual projects.
  • Client segments: collectors, galleries, institutions, cultural projects and curated spaces with high visual standards.
  • Medium: framed artworks, digital previews and documentation prepared for online and offline presentation.

docs.title: Future Technical Integration
docs.text:
As part of our roadmap, Ciclobeef Studio will incorporate technical layers to:

  • Automate communication and content distribution through Meta platforms.
  • Provide APIs or endpoints to integrate with other systems (backends, dashboards, CRMs).
  • Enable data-driven insights about audience response and campaign performance.

This document serves as a reference point for aligning the artistic vision with the technical roadmap.

docs.title: Ciclobeef Studio – Brand & Style Guide (v0.3.0)
docs.text: This document defines the visual and editorial foundations of the Ciclobeef Studio website and related digital products. It must be followed by anyone who creates or updates UI, documentation, or frontend components.

docs.title: 1. Brand Identity
docs.text: Brand name: Ciclobeef Studio Tagline: High-end art, history and society Primary language of the website: English (international audience)

docs.title: 1.1 Mission
docs.text: To connect people worldwide with historical, political and social narratives through high-end visual art, combining research-based storytelling with premium presentation.

docs.title: 1.2 Vision
docs.text: To become a global reference for curated art pieces that document critical moments of history and society, serving collectors, institutions and cultural projects.

docs.title: 1.3 Core Values
docs.text:
• Elegance – visual and narrative quality in every piece and page.
  • Research – historically informed content, not superficial decoration.
  • Impact – works that invite reflection on culture, conflict and identity.
  • Exclusivity – limited, premium offerings, not mass-produced decor.

docs.title: 2. Color Palette
docs.text:
All UI work must use this palette as the primary reference.

  • Primary: #1A1A1A – Deep black / charcoal
  • Use for: main text, headers, footer background.
  • Secondary (Gold/Bronze): #BFA56D
  • Use for: primary buttons, key accents, call-to-action highlights.
  • Accent (Dark Red): #8B0000
  • Use for: hover states, emphasis, warnings, artistic highlights.
  • Light Background: #F5F5F5
  • Use for: hero sections, cards, separated blocks.
  • Body Background: #FFFFFF
  • Use for: page content area.
  • Neutral Gray: #777777
  • Use for: secondary text, muted labels, metadata.

Rule: Never introduce new brand colors in the UI without updating this guide first.

docs.title: 3.1 Typefaces
docs.text:
• Headings: “Playfair Display”, serif
  • Fallbacks: Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif
  • Body text: “Inter”, sans-serif
  • Fallbacks: "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif

Note: If a given environment does not support the primary fonts, the fallbacks must keep the same tone: elegant serif for headings, clean sans-serif for body text.

docs.title: 3.2 Hierarchy
docs.text:
• H1 (Page title)
  • Font: Playfair Display
  • Size (desktop): ~2.5rem
  • Weight: 700
  • Margin top: 3.5rem
  • H2 (Section title)
  • Font: Playfair Display
  • Size: ~2rem
  • Weight: 600
  • Margin top: 2.5rem
  • Body text
  • Font: Inter
  • Size: 1rem
  • Line height: 1.6
  • Quotes / Emphasis
  • Style: italic
  • Color: #8B0000 when appropriate

Rule: Each page should have exactly one main H1. Subsections use H2/H3 for logical structure, not for visual “boldness only”.

docs.title: 4.1 Primary Button
docs.text:
CSS class: .btn-primary

  • Background: #BFA56D
  • Text color: #FFFFFF
  • Padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem
  • Border radius: 4px
  • Font weight: 600
  • Display: inline-block

Hover state:

  • Background: #8B0000
  • Text color: #FFFFFF (unchanged)

docs.title: 4.2 Links
docs.text:
• Default color: #BFA56D
  • Hover: #8B0000
  • No underline by default; underline allowed for emphasis in long paragraphs.

Links must be meaningful: avoid “click here”; prefer “view our project overview”, etc.

docs.title: 5.1 Page Layout
docs.text:
• Content container:
  • Max width: ~1100px (.container)
  • Horizontal padding: ~1.5rem
  • White space is part of the visual hierarchy: avoid cramming elements.

docs.title: 5.2 Header
docs.text:
Class: .ciclo-header

  • Background: #1A1A1A
  • Text: #FFFFFF
  • Bottom border: 2px solid #BFA56D
  • Contains: logo / brand name and main navigation.

docs.title: 5.3 Footer
docs.text:
Class: .ciclo-footer

  • Background: #1A1A1A
  • Text: #F5F5F5
  • Content: legal notice, contact email, copyright.

docs.title: 6. Images and Art Direction
docs.text:
• Use high-resolution images of artworks, but optimized for web.
  • Max width in hero sections: ~1200px.
  • All images:
  • Must have alt text describing the subject (accessibility).
  • Should use subtle border radius (~6px).
  • Should avoid heavy filters that distort the original art.

Visual tone: serious, reflective, with controlled contrast and sobriety.

docs.title: 7. Spacing Rules
docs.text:
• Base line height: 1.6 for paragraphs.
  • Vertical spacing:
  • Section top margin: 3–4rem on desktop, 2rem on mobile.
  • Paragraph spacing: 1.5rem.
  • Avoid stacking more than 3 different typographic styles in a single block (e.g. bold + italic + color + caps).

docs.title: 8. Versioning
docs.text:
This guide is tied to the web release cycle.

  • v0.1.0 – Initial docs and project setup.
  • v0.2.0 – CI/CD, GitFlow, static site deployed.
  • v0.3.0 – Corporate branding and style guide formalized (this document).
  • v0.4.0 – Planned: backend foundation (FastAPI + Meta Graph API).

Any visual or structural change that affects multiple pages must be reflected in this document and released under a new version tag.

docs.title: 9. GitFlow Workflow Reference
docs.text:
Ciclobeef Studio uses a GitFlow-like branching model:

  • main – production-ready code.
  • develop – integration branch for the next release.
  • feature/* – new work units (e.g. feature/design-v3).
  • release/* – release stabilization branches (e.g. release/0.3.0).
  • Tags – mark published versions (e.g. v0.3.0).

Example flow for this release:

  1. Start feature from develop: feature/design-v3
  2. Merge into develop.
  3. Create release/0.3.0 from develop.
  4. Merge release/0.3.0 into main.
  5. Tag v0.3.0 and deploy.

This model is based on widely documented GitFlow practices adapted for release-based workflows.:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.text: By accessing or using this site, contacting CicloBeef Studio or requesting a quote, you agree to these terms. If you disagree with any part, you should not use our services.

docs.title: 2. Artworks and Made-to-Order Studio Editions
docs.text:
CicloBeef Studio offers cultural artworks and printed studio editions prepared under a quote-based, made-to-order model. Studio editions may be produced through external printing and fulfillment providers after the customer confirms the order.

Artwork previews, mockups, colors, scale and presentation may vary reasonably between screens, materials, sizes and printing processes. This does not limit your rights when a studio edition is defective, damaged, incomplete or otherwise covered by mandatory consumer protections.

docs.title: 3. Quotes, Orders and Payments
docs.text:
Artwork requests are started through Instagram DM or Facebook Page DM. LinkedIn may be used for contracts, professional coordination and related administrative matters. Prices are provided through personalized quotes. A quote may depend on the artwork, studio edition, size, orientation, quantity, destination, shipping conditions, applicable taxes and other order details.

The validity period of each quote will be the period stated in that quote. If no valid quote is accepted, CicloBeef Studio may need to prepare an updated quote before the order can continue.

An order is confirmed when the customer accepts the quote and completes payment through the PayPal payment link sent with the final total for that order. Production begins only after payment confirmation and confirmation of the required order details.

CicloBeef Studio does not provide an automated public checkout. The payment link is sent after the quote is approved and reflects the confirmed total communicated to the customer.

docs.title: 4. Customer Information and Order Review
docs.text:
Before confirming an order, the customer is responsible for reviewing the artwork, studio edition, size, orientation, quantity, name, shipping address, city, postal code, country and any other relevant order details.

If the customer provides an incorrect or incomplete address, rejects a delivery, fails to provide required information or causes a shipment issue, the order may require additional coordination, costs, replacement production or carrier action. This does not remove any mandatory rights that apply under the law.

docs.title: 5. Production, Fulfillment and Delivery
docs.text:
Orders may be produced and fulfilled by external printing, fulfillment and shipping providers. Production and delivery times are estimates unless CicloBeef Studio expressly commits to a specific deadline in writing.

Tracking information will be shared when it is available from the relevant provider or carrier.

Taxes, customs duties, import charges or other destination-based costs may apply when they are required by the destination country or disclosed as part of the order process.

docs.title: 6. Cancellations, Changes and Returns
docs.text:
Because studio editions are produced according to the customer's selected artwork, studio edition, size, orientation and destination details, cancellation or change requests should be made as soon as possible.

If production has not started, CicloBeef Studio will review whether the order can be cancelled or changed. If production has started, cancellation or change options may be limited by the made-to-order process and external provider status.

Any right of withdrawal, return right or exception for customized goods applies only to the extent allowed by applicable law. Nothing in these terms excludes mandatory consumer guarantees or rights.

docs.title: 7. Damaged, Defective, Incomplete or Lost Orders
docs.text:
If an order arrives damaged, defective, incomplete or appears to be lost, please contact CicloBeef Studio as soon as reasonably possible at the email below.

We may request photographs of the studio edition, packaging, label and any visible damage when they are necessary to investigate the issue with the print provider, fulfillment provider or carrier.

Depending on the case, available evidence, provider response and applicable law, the solution may include reprint, replacement, refund or another reasonable remedy.

docs.title: 8. Intellectual Property

All artworks, designs, text, brand materials and cultural visual materials created by CicloBeef Studio or its creators remain the intellectual property of CicloBeef Studio or the relevant rights holder.

Purchasing a printed studio edition does not grant permission to copy, reproduce, resell, distribute, mint, publish or commercially exploit digital files, artwork previews or visual materials without prior written authorization.

docs.title: 9. Limitation of Liability

CicloBeef Studio is not responsible for indirect, incidental or consequential losses arising from use of the website, delays outside its reasonable control or actions of external providers, except where liability cannot legally be excluded.

Nothing in these terms limits or excludes liability, warranties, guarantees or consumer protections that cannot be limited or excluded under applicable law.

  • Missing preload strategy for bubble images.
  • Fragile hero margin-top value.
  • Insufficient responsive media queries.
  • Empty docs/assets/social/preview.png file.

docs.title: Audit Findings — CicloBeef Studio Basic Landing
1. Executive Status
docs.text:
Status: Partially ready.

The landing page has a strong visual identity and a working deployed foundation, but it is not yet complete as a Basic Commercial Landing Page for CoreFlux Studio.

It needs commercial structure, product visibility, conversion clarity, SEO basics, responsive improvements, and technical polish before it can be used as a professional Pack 1 demo.

docs.title: 2. Estimated Completion
docs.text:
Current estimated completion: 40%.

Estimated remaining work: 60%.

This percentage is not a mathematical score from DeepSeek. It is a project-management estimate based on the audit findings and the CoreFlux Studio Basic Landing requirements.

docs.title: 3. Why the Landing Is Not Yet at 100%
docs.text:
The current page communicates a brand idea, but it does not yet complete the commercial journey.

A Basic Commercial Landing Page must allow a visitor to understand the offer, see the product, trust the brand, and contact the business through a clear conversion path.

The current landing still lacks several of these elements.

docs.title: 4. Current Strengths
docs.text:
The project already has:

  1. A deployed public landing page.
  2. A custom domain.
  3. A strong visual identity.
  4. A hero section with emotional brand positioning.
  5. A conversation bubble animation.
  6. Legal pages linked from the landing.
  7. Social icon structure.
  8. Separate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.
  9. MkDocs integration.
  10. GitHub Actions deployment workflow.
  11. Existing image and social asset directories.
  12. A clear opportunity to become a CoreFlux Studio portfolio demo.

docs.title: 5. Critical Gaps
docs.text:
The main blockers are:

  1. No clear product visibility.
  2. No complete commercial page structure.
  3. No dedicated "What We Create" section.
  4. No dedicated "Featured Collections" section.
  5. No clear "How It Works" process.
  6. No visible "Available Formats" section.
  7. No "Why CicloBeef Studio" trust section.
  8. No final "Start Your Request" conversion section.
  9. No visible email contact.
  10. Social links must be verified.
  11. Hero copy is too conceptual.
  12. CTA text is not strong enough for commercial conversion.
  13. No viewport meta tag.
  14. No complete SEO metadata.
  15. No Open Graph metadata.
  16. No favicon link.
  17. Font families referenced in CSS must be loaded properly.
  18. Accessibility needs improvement.
  19. Image alt text must be improved.
  20. Terms content must not overpromise automated payments if they are not implemented.
  21. The current conversation bubble sequence must be treated as a visual explanation, not as a real chatbot.

docs.title: 6. Completion Breakdown
docs.text:
Estimated current completion:

  • Deploy and domain: 85%.
  • Visual identity and assets: 60%.
  • Commercial structure: 25%.
  • Conversion path: 20%.
  • SEO, responsive, and accessibility: 35%.
  • Documentation and QA: 45%.

Weighted project estimate:

  • Current: 40%.
  • Remaining: 60%.

docs.title: 7. Remaining Work by Stage
docs.text:
The remaining 60% should be completed through these stages:

  1. Documentation and audit consolidation: +8%.
  2. Commercial HTML structure: +15%.
  3. Copy and value proposition: +8%.
  4. Contact, CTA, and manual quote process: +10%.
  5. Canva assets and product preview: +9%.
  6. SEO, accessibility, and responsive fixes: +7%.
  7. QA, documentation, and release: +3%.

docs.title: 8. Business Interpretation
docs.text:
The landing page should not become a chatbot, backend application, payment system, or API-connected store in this phase.

The Basic Landing must prove that a static page can:

  • Explain the brand.
  • Show the offer.
  • Build trust.
  • Guide the visitor.
  • Generate a quote request.

This is enough to represent CoreFlux Studio's Pack 1 Basic Landing Page.

docs.title: 9. Technical Interpretation
docs.text:
The next technical work should focus on:

  • docs/index.html for structure and content.
  • docs/style.css for visual sections and responsive behavior.
  • docs/script.js for lightweight interactions only.
  • docs/terms.md for manual payment wording.
  • docs/assets/images/ for product mockups.
  • docs/assets/social/ for Open Graph and social preview assets.

No backend should be added during this stage.

docs.title: 10. Final Finding
docs.text:
CicloBeef Studio can become the first professional CoreFlux Studio Basic Landing demo, but only after completing the missing commercial structure, conversion path, SEO basics, technical polish, and QA.

The next step is to implement the Basic Landing completion backlog without adding advanced features from future combos.

1. Purpose
docs.text:
This document stores the official GenAI audit prompt used to evaluate the CicloBeef Studio landing page as a Basic Commercial Landing Page for CoreFlux Studio.

The goal of the audit is not to build advanced automation yet. The goal is to determine whether the current landing page can become a complete, professional, static commercial landing page that belongs to Pack 1, Level 1: Basic Landing Page.

docs.title: 2. Project Context
docs.text:
CicloBeef Studio is a premium cultural wall art studio focused on historical, social, political, and cultural artwork.

The landing page must communicate a clear commercial offer:

  • What CicloBeef Studio sells.
  • Who the artwork is for.
  • Why the brand feels premium.
  • How a potential customer can request a quote.
  • Why the landing page is commercially useful even without backend, chatbot, payment automation, or APIs.

This landing is also intended to become the first real portfolio demo for CoreFlux Studio's Pack 1: Commercial Landing Pages.

docs.title: 3. Pack 1 Context
docs.text:
CoreFlux Studio Pack 1 contains three landing page levels:

  1. Basic Landing Page.
  2. Medium Landing Page.
  3. Advanced Landing Page.

The current CicloBeef Studio project is only focused on the Basic Landing Page.

The Basic Landing Page must be static, responsive, commercially clear, technically clean, and conversion-oriented.

docs.title: 4. Basic Landing Scope
docs.text:
The Basic Landing Page may include:

  • HTML.
  • CSS.
  • JavaScript.
  • Canva-designed visual assets.
  • Static deployment.
  • Responsive layout.
  • SEO basics.
  • Favicon.
  • Social media links.
  • Email contact.
  • Legal links.
  • Manual quote process.
  • Clear commercial CTA.
  • Product preview sections.
  • Trust sections.
  • Basic accessibility improvements.

docs.title: 5. Out of Scope
docs.text:
The Basic Landing Page must not include:

  • Backend.
  • FastAPI.
  • Django.
  • Database.
  • Google Sheets.
  • Google Apps Script.
  • Automated email workflows.
  • Chatbot.
  • LangChain.
  • LangGraph.
  • RAG.
  • Stripe integration.
  • PayPal integration.
  • ThePrintSpace API integration.
  • Meta Graph API integration.
  • CRM.
  • Dashboard.
  • Login system.
  • Payment automation.
  • Quote automation.

Those features belong to future CoreFlux Studio combos or higher-level packs.

docs.title: 6. Audit Role
docs.text:
Act as:

  • Principal Fullstack Software Engineer.
  • UX Strategist.
  • Conversion Rate Optimization Specialist.
  • SaaS Product Architect.
  • Technical Product Manager.

Do not evaluate the landing only as a visual page. Evaluate it as a commercial product that must be sellable as a CoreFlux Studio service.

docs.title: 8. Audit Criteria
docs.text: Evaluate the landing page according to these criteria:

docs.title: 8.1 Business Clarity
docs.text:
Check whether the visitor understands:

  • What CicloBeef Studio sells.
  • Who the offer is for.
  • Why the artwork is premium.
  • Why it is different from generic decoration.
  • How the customer can start the order process.

docs.title: 8.2 Value Proposition
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • Hero headline.
  • Hero subtitle.
  • Product category clarity.
  • Emotional positioning.
  • Cultural positioning.
  • Commercial positioning.
  • CTA quality.

docs.title: 8.3 Conversion Path
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • Primary CTA.
  • Secondary CTA.
  • Final CTA.
  • Email visibility.
  • Social media links.
  • Quote request process.
  • Whether the page can convert a visitor into a real commercial conversation.

docs.title: 8.4 UX/UI
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • Visual hierarchy.
  • Typography.
  • Section spacing.
  • CTA visibility.
  • Mobile layout.
  • Desktop layout.
  • Background usage.
  • Logo placement.
  • Chat bubble animation.
  • Footer clarity.
  • Premium brand perception.

docs.title: 8.5 Technical Quality
docs.text:
Evaluate:

  • HTML semantics.
  • CSS maintainability.
  • JavaScript simplicity.
  • Responsive foundations.
  • SEO metadata.
  • Open Graph metadata.
  • Favicon.
  • Font imports.
  • Accessibility.
  • Alt text.
  • ARIA labels.
  • Performance risks.
  • Image optimization.

docs.title: 8.6 Scope Discipline
docs.text:
Classify every recommendation into one of the following categories:

A. Must be implemented now for Basic Landing completion. B. Should be implemented soon but still belongs to Basic Landing. C. Belongs to Combo 2: Landing + Leads. D. Belongs to Combo 3: Landing + Basic ChatBot. E. Belongs to future API, automation, AI, or advanced services. F. Should not be implemented.

docs.title: 9. Expected Output
docs.text:
Return the audit in this structure:

  1. Executive Decision.
  2. Current Strengths.
  3. Critical Gaps.
  4. Basic Landing Completion Checklist.
  5. Recommended Final Page Structure.
  6. Copywriting Recommendations.
  7. UX/UI Recommendations.
  8. Technical Recommendations.
  9. What Must Stay Out of the Basic Pack.
  10. Canva Workflow Recommendations.
  11. Prioritized Implementation Backlog.
  12. Final Commercial Verdict.

docs.title: 10. Language Rule
docs.text:
The audit output should use English for technical, code, copywriting, branch, and implementation terms.

The project owner may receive strategic explanation in Spanish outside this prompt, but the landing page itself and implementation documentation must remain aligned with an international English-language brand.

docs.title: 6. What CicloBeef Studio Sells
docs.text:
CicloBeef Studio sells premium cultural artwork as wall art and print-based visual pieces.

The offer should be communicated through curated product lines such as:

  • Historical Memory Prints.
  • Political Reflection Artwork.
  • Social Commentary Collections.
  • Custom Cultural Pieces.

These names may evolve, but the landing must clearly show that CicloBeef Studio sells artwork, not only ideas or abstract branding.

docs.title: 7. Target Customer
docs.text:
The Basic Landing should speak to:

  1. Collectors interested in cultural or historical artwork.
  2. Offices that want meaningful and premium wall decoration.
  3. Homes that want conversation-starting visual pieces.
  4. Cultural spaces and studios.
  5. Buyers who value history, society, politics, and visual storytelling.
  6. International customers who are willing to request a quote before buying.

docs.title: 8. Customer Desire
docs.text:
The customer does not only want decoration.

The customer wants:

  • Meaning.
  • Visual impact.
  • Cultural identity.
  • Historical depth.
  • A premium object.
  • A piece that can start conversations.
  • A stronger emotional and intellectual relationship with their space.

docs.title: 9. Brand Tone
docs.text:
The landing tone should be:

  • Premium.
  • Cultural.
  • Direct.
  • Editorial.
  • Serious.
  • Modern.
  • International.
  • Clear.

The landing should avoid:

  • Generic decoration language.
  • Excessive poetry without commercial clarity.
  • Overpromising automation.
  • Overcomplicated technical language.
  • Too many product options.
  • Unverified price promises.

docs.title: 10. Product Formats for Basic Landing
docs.text:
The Basic Landing should present a limited, clear product structure.

Recommended public-facing formats:

  1. Essential Cultural Print — 30 x 40 cm.
  2. Signature Cultural Print — 40 x 60 cm.
  3. Collector Cultural Print — 60 x 80 cm.
  4. Gallery Quote — 70 x 100 cm, available by custom quote.

Important: Prices should not be published yet in the Basic Landing.

Reason: Final pricing depends on print size, material, finish, frame option, destination country, shipping cost, provider availability, exchange rate, taxes, payment fees, and business margin.

docs.title: 11. Manual Quote Model
docs.text:
The Basic Landing should explain that the customer can request a personalized quote.

Recommended customer process:

  1. Choose a collection or artwork style.
  2. Select a preferred size or format.
  3. Send an email or social media message.
  4. Receive a personalized quote.
  5. Approve the quote.
  6. Receive manual payment instructions.
  7. The artwork is produced and shipped through a professional fine art fulfillment workflow.

docs.title: 12. Payment Positioning
docs.text:
The Basic Landing must not promise automated checkout.

Recommended wording:

Payments are processed after a personalized quote has been approved. CicloBeef Studio may provide manual payment instructions depending on the customer's location and the available payment method.

Possible future manual payment methods may include:

  • PayPal.
  • Stripe Payment Links.
  • Wise.
  • Bank transfer.
  • Other region-specific payment methods.

These should not be described as an automated integrated checkout until the payment flow is actually implemented.

docs.title: 13. Provider Positioning
docs.text:
The landing may mention professional fine art fulfillment partners in a general way.

The landing should not yet describe ThePrintSpace API, automatic order creation, automated shipping calculation, or automated tracking as active Basic Landing features.

ThePrintSpace replacement of WhiteWall should be documented internally, but the Basic Landing should only communicate the customer-facing result:

  • Premium print production.
  • Professional fulfillment.
  • Quote-based ordering.
  • Size and finish availability subject to quote confirmation.

docs.title: 14. What the Landing Sells Now
docs.text:
The Basic Landing sells:

  • A premium artwork concept.
  • Curated cultural print collections.
  • Manual quote requests.
  • Direct contact with CicloBeef Studio.
  • A professional first commercial experience.

docs.title: 15. What the Landing Does Not Sell Yet
docs.text:
The Basic Landing does not sell:

  • Automated checkout.
  • Dynamic quote calculation.
  • Live inventory.
  • API-based fulfillment.
  • Customer accounts.
  • CRM-managed orders.
  • Chatbot-guided purchases.
  • Automatic payment links.
  • Automatic shipping calculation.
  • Real-time provider integration.

docs.title: 16. Commercial CTA Strategy
docs.text:
Primary CTA:

See Our Collections

Secondary CTA:

Request Your Quote

Final CTA:

Start Your Request

Recommended final CTA copy:

Email us with your preferred collection, size, framing option, and destination country. We will send you a personalized quote before production.

docs.title: 17. Commercial Objective
docs.text:
The Basic Landing must convert a visitor into a commercial conversation.

The goal is not automatic sale yet.

The goal is:

Visitor -> understands offer -> sees product direction -> understands process -> requests quote.
